skipped_entirely.name: data/mechanisms/salience/grounding_A_main (FULL_G / NO_NEWS_G)
skipped_entirely.reason: Verified directly by inspecting every session's trace: in this corpus the price-tool readings are injected as static text in the user prompt (grounding='price-tool-readings block injected'), so the agent's tool_calls contain only submit_decision in the overwhelming majority of sessions (1,998/2,000); a full rescan (corrected 2026-10-23 after independent verification) found 2/2,000 sessions additionally call get_risk_budget (a different tool, also never get_volatility_stats). get_volatility_stats specifically is never invoked as a tool anywhere in this corpus (0/2,000). The task's own inclusion rule ('get_volatility_stats was called at least once') therefore yields exactly 0 usable sessions here, confirmed on all 2000 session files, not inferred from a sample. This corpus cannot test tool-output copying by construction and is reported as skipped, not substituted with a weaker proxy.

examples.note: Model names the figure 'annualized' (get_volatility_stats ann_vol_20d_pct=16.4) and ~20 lines later calls it 'approximately 16% annually', then submits expected_vol_pct=16.4 -- the exact annualised number -- as the 5-day forecast. Rational 5-day sigma for this day was 3.37%; realised 5-day vol (panel) was 3.74%.
quotes: Volatility remains subdued at approximately 16% annually.

examples.note: Model reads 'Recent volatility is elevated (33.5-36.5% annualized)' from the tool output, restates it as 'elevated volatility in the 30% range' right before the forecast, and submits expected_vol_pct=30.0 -- close to ann_vol_20d_pct=30.1, not to a correctly-scaled 5-day figure. Rational 5-day sigma was 4.67%; realised 5-day vol (panel) was 5.34%.
quotes: Recent volatility is elevated (33.5-36.5% annualized), but regime is "normal"
My forecast anticipates modest gains around 0.8% with elevated volatility in the 30% range, reflecting the stock's current dynamic price environment.

examples.note: Same ticker/day as the k=1 rollout below (HWM_2026-03-27), where get_volatility_stats reported 'Volatility: 31-34% annualized, normal regime'. This rollout (k=3) anchors on that annualised band and submits expected_vol_pct=27.0 (looks-copied: within 15% of ann_vol_20d_pct=31.3). Rational 5-day sigma=5.62%; realised 5-day vol=6.24%.
quotes: I anticipate volatility between 25-30%, suggesting cautious optimism about near-term price dynamics.

examples.note: Model explicitly de-annualises ann_vol_20d_pct=28.4 with the sqrt(time) rule (28.4/sqrt(252)=1.77%/day, *sqrt(5)=3.95%) and submits expected_vol_pct=4.0, matching its own correct arithmetic almost exactly.
quotes: expected_vol_pct: Volatility is high at 28.4% annualized, so 5-day vol would be roughly sqrt(5) * daily vol. Daily vol ≈ 28.4%/sqrt(252) ≈ 1.77%. 5-day vol ≈ 1.77% * sqrt(5) ≈ 3.95%

examples.note: Same ticker/day as the k=3 rollout above; this rollout (k=1) correctly applies the sqrt(5) scaling to the same 31-34% annualised reading and submits expected_vol_pct=13.0 (within the 12-15% it computed). Shows the literal-copy failure is a per-rollout sampling event, not a fixed property of the ticker/day.
quotes: expected_vol_pct: With 31-34% annualized volatility, 5-day vol is roughly sqrt(5) times daily, or about 12-15% one-standard-deviation

examples.note: First pass mis-derives daily vol (uses sqrt(1/20) instead of sqrt(1/252)), reaches 14.3% for the 5-day figure and rejects it as implausible. Second pass restates the metric definition correctly and redoes the conversion properly, landing on 4.07% -- yet two sentences later writes 'let me estimate expected_vol_pct around 6-8% to be conservative' and finally submits expected_vol_pct=6.5, ~60% above its own correctly-computed number. Trace (4.07%) and submitted answer (6.5%) do not match.
quotes: Wait, expected_vol_pct is the one-standard-deviation size of the 5-day return in percent. Given annualized vol of ~28.9% over 20 days, daily vol would be ~sqrt(1/20)*28.9% = ~6.4% per day. Over 5 days, volatility accumulates as sqrt(5)*6.4% ≈ 14.3%. But that seems high.

Actually, the expected_vol_pct parameter is "one-standard-deviation size of the 5-day return, percent (not annualised, not daily)". So if daily return has std dev of X%, 5-day return would have std dev of X% * sqrt(5).

Given 20-day annualized vol of 28.9%, daily vol ≈ 28.9% / sqrt(252) ≈ 1.82% per day. Over 5 days: 1.82% * sqrt(5) ≈ 4.07%.

limitations_and_open_questions: The grounding_20261012/A_main corpus could not be used at all for this mechanism (0/2000 sessions call get_volatility_stats); the salience-copying question remains untested in that price-grounded setting.

q3news_S1 cross-check N is small (155 FULL / 139 NO_NEWS) because most sessions in that corpus never call get_volatility_stats; its regression coefficients are noisy (wide SEs) and should be read as directionally consistent with newsagent, not as independent confirmation at comparable precision.

The 'looks-copied' group size (12-27 sessions depending on split) is too small to further stratify by ticker, volatility regime, or k without very wide uncertainty; this is reported as an open question, not resolved here.

Model 2's b1 estimate is unstable across corpora (0.57-0.62 in newsagent vs 0.06-0.40 in q3news, overlapping confidence given q3news's wide SE of ~0.85) -- NOT claimed as a cross-model finding, just noted.

This analysis treats each (day_id, k) rollout as an independent observation for OLS/SE purposes; days contribute up to 4 correlated rollouts (same ticker/day, different sampling draws), so classical SEs here are a lower bound on the true SE under day-level clustering. Reported both classical and HC1-robust SEs; neither corrects for within-day clustering specifically. This does not change the sign of any headline conclusion (b2~0 either way) but means the step-3 group-size CIs would widen somewhat under day clustering.

rational_benchmark_join.method: day_id (TICKER_date) looked up as event_id in events_all.parquet first; misses fell back to nonevent_days.parquet joined on ticker+t (sigma = exp(lsig) there). Checked explicitly which corpus day_ids are events_all misses (6/250 newsagent day_ids: CSGP_2026-03-31, ED_2026-03-12, GLW_2026-03-12, GWW_2026-06-16, IDXX_2026-08-04, PG_2026-03-12) and confirmed all 6 are present in nonevent_days.
rational_benchmark_join.sigma_scale_conversion: No numeric conversion needed, and this is verified rather than assumed: data/mechanisms/salience/rcf_20261011/rule.json field 'operationalization.target_and_bins' states R5 = 100*ln(C[t+5]/C[t]) (the realised 5-day log return, in percent) and sigma = exp(lsig), both evaluated at close t, with u=(R5-m)/sigma. So events_all.sigma IS ALREADY the rational model's standard deviation of the 5-day percent log return -- same units (percent) and same horizon (5 trading days) as the agent's submitted expected_vol_pct. Used directly, unscaled, as rational_sigma5_pct in the regression below.

realised_5d_vol_method.definition: rv5_realised_pct = sqrt(sum of the 5 squared daily log returns in percent, close t to close t+5) from data/panel/us_daily_stratos_20260924.parquet, matching the project's own rv5 definition in the research workspace's repro/rsize/rules_doc.py ('sqrt of the sum of the 5 squared daily log returns (percent)').
realised_5d_vol_method.validation: For AAPL_2026-03-19, summing the 5 panel daily log returns from 2026-03-19 to 2026-03-26 reproduces events_all.R5 = 1.566235 to 6 decimal places (1.5662345352...), confirming date alignment and close-price series match between the panel and the benchmark.
realised_5d_vol_method.why_rv5_not_abs_R5: events_all.R5 is a SIGNED 5-day return, not a volatility measure; sqrt(sum of squared daily returns) is the more faithful realised-volatility proxy and is exactly the quantity this project's own code already calls rv5 -- used instead of the noisier |R5| single-path proxy for the accuracy metric in step 3.

step2_regression_ols.headline_finding: In the primary corpus (newsagent FULL, n=694), b1 (rational 5-day sigma) is strongly significant (0.566, SE 0.069, t=8.17) and model 1 R2=0.0880. Adding ann_vol_20d_pct (model 2) moves b2 to -0.0073 (SE 0.0205, t=-0.36, not significant) and R2 to only 0.0881 -- delta R2 = 0.00017, i.e. essentially no additional linear explanatory power from the annualised headline number once the rational benchmark is in the regression. The same near-zero, non-significant b2 pattern holds in NO_NEWS (b2=+0.0047, SE 0.0210) and in the much smaller q3news FULL cross-check (b2=-0.0433, SE 0.1016). CONCLUSION: the AGGREGATE linear test finds no detectable smooth anchoring effect of ann_vol_20d_pct on top of the rational sigma. This does not mean salience-copying is absent -- see step 3, which finds a concentrated, rare, discrete failure mode that a linear-in-the-whole-sample regression is not well suited to detect.
step2_regression_ols.spec: expected_vol_pct ~ a + b1*rational_sigma5_pct   [model 1]   and expected_vol_pct ~ a + b1*rational_sigma5_pct + b2*ann_vol_20d_pct   [model 2]. Closed-form OLS via numpy normal equations (no scipy/statsmodels in the venv -- confirmed absent). SE = classical OLS (homoskedastic) standard errors; se_hc1 = heteroskedasticity-robust (HC1 sandwich) SE also reported as a robustness check. p-values use a normal approximation to the t-distribution (fine given dof in the hundreds).

step3_copied_vs_not_copied.accuracy_metric: abs(ln(expected_vol_pct / rv5_realised_pct)) -- absolute log-ratio error against the panel-computed realised 5-day vol (see realised_5d_vol_method); restricted to sessions with rv5_realised_pct > 0.
step3_copied_vs_not_copied.definition: looks_copied = |expected_vol_pct - ann_vol_20d_pct| / ann_vol_20d_pct <= 0.15 (within 15% of the annualised headline figure -- effectively requires the agent to have reported ~7x too much vol relative to the correct sqrt-time-scaled 5-day figure, since ann_vol_20d_pct / 7.1 is roughly what a correct 5-day conversion would give).
step3_copied_vs_not_copied.headline_finding: The looks-copied group is RARE (FULL: 15/694 = 2.16%; NO_NEWS: 12/751 = 1.60%; combined: 27/1445 = 1.87%) but has dramatically worse forecast accuracy: mean abs-log-ratio-error combined = 1.73 (SE 0.126) for the copied group vs 0.62 (SE 0.012) for everyone else -- a difference of 1.11 (SE 0.127, t=8.78), huge and precisely estimated despite n=27 because the effect size is large (e^1.73≈5.6x vs e^0.62≈1.9x typical multiplicative miss). Consistent in FULL alone (diff=1.10, SE 0.172, t=6.39, n_copied=15) and NO_NEWS alone (diff=1.13, SE 0.195, t=5.82, n_copied=12). CAVEAT: n_copied is small in every split (12-27); the point estimate of the group SIZE is noisy even though the point estimate of the accuracy GAP is not (because within-group variance, not n, sets that SE).
step3_copied_vs_not_copied.reconciliation_with_step2: Step 2's regression found no smooth linear anchoring effect; step 3 finds a strong, real effect concentrated in a small (~2%) subgroup that nearly literally copies the annualised number. These are not contradictory: salience-copying here looks like a rare DISCRETE failure (full copy or no copy), not a graded bias that shifts everyone's forecast a little -- a linear regression averaged over ~98% unaffected sessions will correctly find ~zero slope even when a sharp, large, real failure mode exists in the tail.

copy_rate_two_proportion_test.note: two-proportion z-test on the 'looks-copied' (within 15% of ann_vol_20d_pct) rate; small k makes this low-powered.

step5_full_vs_nonews_salience_effect.headline_finding: Neither the regression b2 (FULL -0.0073 vs NO_NEWS +0.0047, diff -0.0120, SE 0.0293, t=-0.41) nor the looks-copied RATE (FULL 2.16% vs NO_NEWS 1.60%, diff +0.56pp, SE 0.71pp, z=0.79, p~0.43) differs significantly between arms. Both comparisons are LOW-POWERED (b2 itself is indistinguishable from 0 in both arms; the copying rate is based on only 12-15 events per arm), so this is best read as 'no evidence of a difference', not 'confirmed no difference'. At face value it is consistent with the project's established finding that price-tool salience operates largely independently of whether news is also in context -- the literal-copy failure mode shows up at a similar (small) rate whether or not news competes for attention.

task: SALIENCE: does the size of a conspicuous annualised-volatility number the agent sees (get_volatility_stats tool output) predict its 5-day expected_vol_pct forecast beyond what the rational benchmark (events_all.parquet sigma) justifies?
